evidence.title: When is a real estate project exempt from RERA registration?
evidence.property_name: When is a real estate project exempt from RERA registration?
evidence.description: Title: When is a real estate project exempt from RERA registration? When is a real estate project exempt from RERA registration? # When is a real estate project exempt from RERA registration? Not every real estate project in India needs registration with the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (RERA). real estate projects exempt from RERA registration. + Is RERA registration mandatory for all projects? + Can I file a complaint if the project is exempt from RERA? + How do I verify if a project is RERA-registered? The project registration with the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (RERA) has become a key benchmark for trust in real estate, offering buyers legal protection and transparency. While RERA mandates registration for most real estate projects, the law also outlines clear exceptions. If the development area is 500 sq m or smaller, and the total number of proposed apartments, including all phases, is eight or fewer, the project is exempt from RERA registration, as per Section 3(2)(a) of the Act. For instance, a standalone building with six apartments on a 400 sq m plot is exempt from registration. According to Section 3(2)(b) of the Act, RERA registration is not required if a project involves only renovation, repair, or redevelopment, and does not include new advertising, marketing, selling, or allotment. Under Section 3 of the RERA Act, 2016, all residential and commercial real estate projects exceeding 500 sq m or comprising more than eight units must be registered with the respective State RERA authority before being advertised or sold. Understanding when RERA registration is not mandatory helps both buyers and developers avoid legal confusion. Is RERA registration mandatory for all projects? Can I file a complaint if the project is exempt from RERA? **A.** No. If a project is legally exempt, RERA may not entertain your complaint. RERA rules for housing societies.
